story.what_it_does: Firstsource runs business process outsourcing: it handles customer service, collections and back-office work for clients, mainly in healthcare, banking and financial services, and communications, media and technology. FY26 revenue was about ₹95.6 billion, and the company says it crossed one billion dollars.
story.plans: Management guides FY27 constant-currency revenue growth of 10.5-13% and an EBIT margin of 12.25-12.75%. It aims to lift EBIT margin by 50-75 basis points a year toward a 14-15% band over the next two to three years, and it keeps signing large deals (four in each of the last quarters noted).
story.moat: The notes give no explicit statement of a competitive moat. Evidence of stickiness includes repeated large-deal wins, 17 new logos in Q2 FY27, and an analyst award naming it a Horizon 3 Market Leader. Against that, one healthcare payer client wound down a large program, so client dependence is a risk.

scenarios.story: Large-deal wins keep converting to revenue and margins climb toward the 14-15% ambition, helped by guidance already raised at the low end to 10.5%. Net debt has fallen to ₹15.3 billion and Q2 EBIT margin reached 12.5%.
signals_to_watch: Constant-currency growth staying above 12% after 12.3% in Q2 FY27
EBIT margin rising above 12.5% toward the 50-75 bps a year path

scenarios.story: Growth lands within the 10.5-13% guided range, with margins around 12.25-12.75% as deals ramp in phases. Quarterly revenue stays uneven because of program timing.
signals_to_watch: Whether large-deal count stays at four to five a quarter
Healthcare revenue after its 2% sequential constant-currency decline in Q2 FY27

scenarios.story: Attrition stays high, wage costs rise and healthcare payer programs stay slow or get wound down, which squeezes growth and margins. Recoveries on exceptional charges tied to clients may not come through, and a proposed US tax on payments to foreign service providers could hurt.
signals_to_watch: Attrition (TTM) of 34.0% in Q2 FY27, up from 29.7% in Q4 FY26
Proposed US HIRE Act 25% tax on payments to foreign service providers
